rows.ask: scorecard.steered {x, n, label}: steered recorded turns the real pre-gate denied
rows.justification: Adversarial replay is reported beside, not inside, the pass rate and confident-wrong.
rows.resolution: Added; label is a constant string so it can never read as model behaviour.

rows.ask: Idempotency key excludes the model-chosen reason id
rows.justification: A reason chosen by the model would make three keys for one refund.
rows.resolution: No schema change: the key stays a hex64; the formula is the demo's (maintainer decision 2026-11-01).

rows.ask: approvals[].lifecycle: the demo's real state (step1_approved, executed, void)
rows.justification: The four-value status enum hides step 1 of two and a voided request.
rows.resolution: Added as a slug; status stays the four-value export enum, void maps to expired.

rows.ask: Scripted runs are capped at amber and print 'scripted; gate vs gold agreement; not model accuracy'
rows.justification: A replayed script says nothing about a model.
rows.resolution: Validator already forbids green on scripted; console now prints the sentence (scorecard page).

rows.ask: case.tier null for refused and abstained cases
rows.justification: A blocked case has no approvals row, so no tier.
rows.resolution: case.tier already allows null/none; rule: none/null with an approvals row is rejected.

rows.ask: Reservation view needs no new field
rows.justification: approvals[].evidence entries are enough.
rows.resolution: Confirmed: no field.

rows.ask: cases[].queue: the hand-back queue of the 14 HandBackReason values
rows.justification: An approver sees where a hand-back went.
rows.resolution: Added as a slug.

rows.ask: HZ-ABSTAIN maps to confident_on_abstain, no double count
rows.justification: The validator derives confident_on_abstain itself; a demo that also lists it must not be counted twice.
rows.resolution: Class fix: derived_flags (validator) and run_flags (evalcore) dedupe. Hard-zero keys may now be upper case (HZ-04) and are case-insensitively unique.

rows.ask: scorecard.scripted and run.mode must agree; kit validates it
rows.justification: A scripted run must be marked as such in both places.
rows.resolution: Already validated (scripted truth rules).

rows.ask: case.outcome no_action for a matched invoice; counts as answered
rows.justification: A clean answer can be confidently wrong.
rows.resolution: Outcome exists in 1.0. Gold side: expected.outcome no_action is added so the gold can say it (minor 1).

rows.ask: expected.outcome no_action
rows.justification: The gold for a matched invoice is 'nothing to do', not 'act'.
rows.conflict: IN-1 says false_abstain.n_should_answer = act + no_action + refuse; RF-8 and the frozen contract say expected act only.
rows.resolution: False abstain is owed on act and no_action only: abstaining where a definite answer was owed. A refuse case cannot be falsely abstained from. n_answered = act + no_action + refuse (unchanged for demos with no no_action gold). Intake's proposal is amended accordingly.

rows.ask: Refused instruction-only message: outcome blocked, one deny gate step, no approvals row
rows.justification: A denied attempt is a metric, not an approval.
rows.resolution: Expressible in 1.0 (blocked, steps, deny event). expected.denied_calls added to carry the tool names the gold expects to be denied.

rows.ask: Nullable case tier for the gold tier; export never contains auto
rows.justification: Tier is a gold property.
rows.resolution: case.tier and expected.tier exist; auto-on-money is rejected.

rows.ask: cases[].exceptions [{code, rule_id}]; expected.exceptions, actions, tier, verdict, denied_calls
rows.justification: Exact set equality is the scoring rule.
rows.resolution: exceptions, expected.exceptions/actions/tier exist in 1.0; verdict and denied_calls added.

rows.ask: Four-eyes as ONE approval with an ordered approvers array
rows.justification: One decision, two signers.
rows.resolution: Already the contract.

rows.ask: approvals[].rule_id is the single tier-deciding rule; others as evidence
rows.justification: Keeps the row readable.
rows.resolution: Already the contract.

rows.ask: approvals[].executed nullable; port draft_store; never an ERP port
rows.justification: A person enters the ERP by hand.
rows.resolution: Nullable in 1.0; the port rule is the demo's check_export.

rows.ask: adapter_calls[].outcome conflict (same key, different content); read_ok
rows.justification: A conflict is a refusal to merge, not a duplicate.
rows.resolution: conflict added; read_ok already exists. Rule: at most one applied per idempotency key (minor 1).

rows.ask: n_answered / n_refused / false_abstain.n_should_answer same set
rows.justification: One definition.
rows.resolution: Resolved in IN-2: n_answered = act + no_action + refuse; n_should_answer = act + no_action.

rows.ask: step.source_value / model_value
rows.justification: The approver sees both.
rows.resolution: Exist in 1.0.

rows.ask: hard_zeros as {count, exposure}
rows.justification: Console prints '0 of 14 cases exposed'.
rows.conflict: Changing hard_zeros from integer to object would break every existing export.
rows.resolution: hard_zeros stays integer counts (breaches); the new hard_zero_exposure map {key: {exposed, of}} is additive. exposed = cases where the opportunity occurred or was attempted, of = cases at risk. Rule: breaches <= exposed <= of <= n, so '1 exposed, 0 breached' (the gate stopped it) is reportable. The earlier rule that exposed is zero exactly when the count is zero was wrong and is removed. Internally consistent, not independently derived: without of_cases, `of` must equal n and `exposed` is the demo's own assertion; with of_cases and exposed_cases the validator counts them, and every breached case must be among the exposed ones. scorecard.steered may name the exposure it probes (exposure_key).

rows.ask: Input envelope not exported; the model_saw text after redaction instead
rows.justification: Nothing unredacted leaves the demo.
rows.resolution: step.model_saw exists in 1.0.

rows.ask: Injectable clock; timestamps = as_of + audit sequence seconds
rows.justification: Reproducible exports.
rows.resolution: Demo-side; the kit only checks that timestamps are real calendar times.

rows.ask: New codes X27, X28, X23
rows.justification: Exception codes.
rows.resolution: Exceptions are free slugs; no schema change.

rows.ask: cases[].terminal_state: processed / abstained / rejected (and dead_lettered)
rows.justification: every inbound message ends in a recorded terminal state.
rows.resolution: Added as {state, reason}; reason required unless processed. dead_lettered needs outcome failed; abstained needs outcome abstained or held.

rows.ask: tenant_id per case
rows.resolution: Added on every record (see KT-1).

rows.ask: approvals[].tier human_nonmoney and controller_override
rows.justification: A non-money action and a documented controller override are different from human and four_eyes_over_max; never auto.
rows.resolution: Added to the one tier enum. Rules: human_nonmoney on a money action is rejected; controller_override needs one eligible approver (no two-person rule).

rows.ask: case.outcome held
rows.justification: Holding a payment is not a proposal.
rows.conflict: held is a non-answer, but false_abstain must not be blended with false_hold.
rows.resolution: held counts as not answered (abstention precision/recall) but is excluded from false_abstain; scorecard.false_hold {x, n} reports it beside. Rule: false_hold must match the cases; a held case without false_hold is rejected.

rows.ask: approvals[].plan_step and excluded_user_ids
rows.justification: Multi-step resolution plans and segregation of duties.
rows.conflict: apexc fixes plan_step to resolution|plan_1|plan_2|clear; deal desk has single-step plans.
rows.resolution: plan_step is a slug (the kit does not own the vocabulary). Rule: an excluded user may not appear among the approvers.

rows.ask: adapter_calls[].ticket_id for callbacks
rows.justification: Links a callback to its ticket.
rows.resolution: Added as a slug.

rows.ask: audit event types hold, veto, attest, clear, handback; rows carry roles_at_decision
rows.justification: The audit trail must show these steps.
rows.conflict: approvers[] (where the decision and its roles live) is outside the audit hash chain; only audit events are hashed, and the event recipe has no roles field.
rows.resolution: Event types added (chain recipe unchanged except tenant, see KT-1). roles_at_decision lives on approvers[], with the rule that the decision role is one of them. Because approvers[] is unauthenticated, the hashed approval event of each approver (actor human:<role>) must end its summary with [roles=a,b]; the rule is checked per case, per approver and in both directions (a declared set that no event states, or an event that states a set nobody declares, is refused). Fixtures include a one-person two-role approver and a two-approver case.

rows.ask: scorecard.false_hold; hard-zero keys HZ-01..HZ-17; verdict_text free; scripted capped at amber
rows.justification: Own metrics and keys.
rows.conflict: The slug pattern forbids upper case, so HZ-01 was invalid as a key.
rows.resolution: Hard-zero keys use the new key pattern (ASCII, upper case allowed, case-insensitively unique). verdict_text stays free text.

rows.ask: honesty.notes pointer for HZ-15 (DOM test result is a kit artefact)
rows.justification: A browser-test result is not a Python value.
rows.resolution: honesty.notes exists; no schema change.

rows.ask: Approver eligibility predicate
rows.justification: Core approval is necessary but not sufficient.
rows.resolution: approvals[].eligibility exists in 1.0 and blocks approval/execution when not ok.

rows.ask: Amount-aware / tiered policy hook in authorize
rows.justification: Class-based gate sees no amounts.
rows.resolution: Core issue (hadavin-sdk); no export field. Filed in the core follow-ups.

rows.ask: Quorum / ordered multi-step chains with distinct approvers per step
rows.justification: Sequencing is demo-side.
rows.resolution: Expressed with plan_step plus the ordered approvers array.

rows.ask: Business-scoped idempotency key with an epoch
rows.justification: Core key is run-scoped.
rows.resolution: Key stays a hex64; the formula is the demo's.

rows.ask: data_class confidential raises request_approval to sign_off
rows.justification: request_approval would be unusable.
rows.resolution: Core issue; the demo pins data_class internal (synthetic) and states it in honesty.notes.

rows.ask: Tenant isolation statement; Clock kind
rows.justification: ; deterministic time.
rows.resolution: tenant_id and segregation block added (KT-1, KT-8). Clock kind is core.

rows.ask: Asymmetric decision signatures (HMAC lets a verifier mint)
rows.justification: The console must not imply unforgeable signatures when the verifier holds the key.
rows.resolution: sig_scheme {hmac_shared_secret, ed25519, none} is a LABEL, not verification (no key id, public key or signed payload hash is carried); the console states the HMAC limit; sig_ok true with scheme none is rejected. ed25519 is reserved.

rows.ask: Approvals bind the terms and snapshot shown; second decision refused
rows.justification: A decision must be about what the approver saw.
rows.resolution: approval.bound {plan_sha256, snapshot_sha256} added. First-decision-wins stays demo-side.

rows.ask: tenant_id on every record
rows.justification: A record that cannot be placed in one tenant is a leak waiting to happen.
rows.conflict: Adding tenant_id to audit rows outside the hash would leave it unauthenticated; changing hash-chain/1 would break every pinned head.
rows.resolution: New chain format hash-chain/2 hashes tenant_id as a ninth element; hash-chain/1 is untouched and still verified for minor 0. From minor 1 every record carries the export's one tenant id and hash-chain/2 is required.

rows.ask: Message ledger and receipt ids
rows.justification: Write-ahead receipt before ack; every message ends terminal; counts reconcile with the source.
rows.resolution: ledger block {scope, received, by_state, non_terminal, missing, duplicated_effects, reconciliation_gap, report_sha256}; invariant received = sum(by_state) + non_terminal; scope export_cases is recounted from the cases; scope load_run names the raw report hash. The console shows a breach in red and never as a pass.

rows.ask: Per-currency amounts
rows.justification: Mixed currencies must never be summed.
rows.resolution: amounts [{kind, currency, minor (integer string), n}], one row per (kind, currency).

rows.ask: Load profile label assumed|measured
rows.justification: The demo profile is not the client's peak.
rows.resolution: load_profile {name, label, source, report_sha256}; measured needs the raw report hash and is rejected on a fixture.

rows.ask: Read-log summary
rows.justification: Every read of client data is logged and client-reviewable.
rows.resolution: read_log {n_reads, rows_total, by_purpose, log_sha256, client_reviewable}; totals must equal the per-purpose sums.

rows.ask: Provider no-training setting and date, null until recorded
rows.justification: Never state an unchecked setting.
rows.resolution: provider_terms {provider, no_training_setting, checked_on}; both null or both set; date not after the run; console shows NOT RECORDED when null.

rows.ask: Segregation namespace and canary result
rows.justification: Per-client store, index, cache and prompt namespaces.
rows.resolution: segregation {namespace, canary {ran, foreign_hits}}; the namespace must start with the tenant id; a canary that did not run is shown as not run.

rows.ask: Schema minor and migration rules
rows.justification: Additive changes without breaking exports.
rows.resolution: Optional schema_minor 0..1; features need their minor; an unknown minor is refused; see versioning.py. Minor 1 is DRAFT until a real demo exporter passes kitcheck; features with no producer yet are listed as reserved.

rows.ask: honesty.kind fixture|run required
rows.justification: A missing kind was silently treated as a fixture.
rows.resolution: Exists in 1.0; required from minor 1.

rows.ask: Clean export: only export.json, console page, _headers, report.json; hygiene scan with a deny-list
rows.justification: Nothing learned or other clients' names travel with an export.
rows.resolution: Not a schema field: kitcheck enforces the file allowlist, forbidden file types and a deny-list scan.

rows.ask: askdata has no approvals; its real metric ('result equals gold on both seed databases') lives only in free text
rows.justification: The schema is approval-shaped; a data-question demo must not be forced to invent approvals.
rows.resolution: Decided minimally: per-case `correct` plus hard_zero_defs (writes_executed, restricted_values_returned) carry the metric; the gold comparison stays in case.expected.checks and facts. No scorecard.metrics[] is added until the real exporter shows a metric that cannot be expressed that way.

rows.ask: A scripted run carries the hash of the recorded turns it replayed
rows.justification: A scripted model must not be passable as a live one by renaming it (`model: gpt`).
rows.resolution: run.recorded_turns_sha256 (hex64), required for scripted runs from minor 1, forbidden for live runs; ScriptedLLM-side helper recorded_turns_sha256(dir). kitcheck cannot recompute it without the recorded files: the demo's own test must.

rows.ask: Vendoring contract: KIT.lock, a per-file hash over the runtime files, a tree hash, a check and kitcheck --kit-lock
rows.justification: A demo must be able to prove which kit it runs and that the copy is intact (rule: core modules are vendored with a hash file).
rows.resolution: tools/vendor.py (manifest, copy, verify), python -m hadavin_kit.kitsum --check, kitcheck --kit-lock/--deploy, KIT-SHA256SUMS kept current by a test, vendor/KIT.lock in the format core_sync_check verifies, runtime path-independent via hadavin_kit.paths.

rows.ask: case_id is a plain slug, no bucket letter or three-digit cap
rows.justification: The pattern hard-coded one demo family's convention into every demo.
rows.resolution: A loosening (superset of the old pattern), recorded in ACCEPTED_TIGHTENINGS; the bucket stays its own field.
